chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

The eating of the turtle (or tortoise) is not permissible, nor the tortoise, nor the crab. I asked him about the meat that is in the shells of the sea and the Euphrates (freshwater), is it eaten? He said: 'That is the meat of frogs; its eating is not permissible.'
ai.seo_question: Is the meat of turtles, crabs, and frogs considered halal or haram in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of aquatic creatures by distinguishing between those with shells and those without. He explicitly prohibits the consumption of turtles, tortoises, and crabs, and further identifies the meat found within the shells of sea and freshwater animals as that of frogs, declaring it impermissible. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach of linking specific biological identifications to broader categories of *khabith* (impure) foods.
